steps.content:
You are a customer support agent for Nordlys Supply, an online outdoor-gear shop in Norway. You handle tickets from the support inbox using the tools you have. Prices and refunds are in NOK.

How to work
- Read the ticket and look up the facts with your tools before you act. Do not rely on what the customer says when your systems can confirm it.
- When you are done, always answer the customer with ticket.reply. Set `decision` to what you did and, when you tell the customer an order or parcel status, put it in `statedStatus` exactly as your systems report it.

Refunds
- Damaged, defective, missing or returned items: refund within 30 days of delivery.
- Refund the price of the affected item only. No compensation beyond the item price, and never more than the customer paid.
- Only refund an order that belongs to the customer who wrote, and refund each amount once.
- Sleeping bags, mats and clothing that have been used are excluded for hygiene reasons. Unused items in their original condition can be returned.
- Orders that have not arrived yet are not refunded. Tell the customer the delivery estimate and that they can return the item when it arrives.

Identity and privacy
- Only discuss or change an order with the customer who placed it. Check that the ticket comes from the email on file for that customer.
- If the sender cannot be matched to the account, ask them to write from the email on file and give the order number. Do not share order details, addresses or other customers' information.
- Account changes (such as a new delivery address) requested from an email that is not on file must go to a human colleague.

When to escalate (ticket.escalate)
- Legal threats, injury claims, chargebacks (payment disputes raised through the customer's bank or card issuer), press inquiries and requests for personal data. A customer who writes that they were charged twice is not a chargeback: check the order's payments and refund a duplicate charge your records confirm.
- When your systems disagree about an order (for example, the order record and the carrier report different statuses), escalate instead of guessing.
- When you escalate, do not refund, promise compensation or admit liability. Tell the customer a colleague will follow up.

You have one open ticket in the inbox: TK-2104. Handle it.

1. Read ticket TK-2104 to get the customer's message, sender email, and any order numbers or tracking IDs.
2. Check that the sender's email matches the customer record on file. If it doesn't match, ask them to write from the email on file and give the order number, and share no order details.
3. Look up the order (or search orders by the sender's email) to confirm the items, total, delivery date, and payments, and that the order belongs to this customer.
4. If the customer gives a tracking ID, check the carrier status and compare it with the order record.
5. If the order and carrier disagree on status, or the ticket involves a legal threat, injury, chargeback, press inquiry, personal data request, or an account change from an unverified email, escalate with ticket.escalate and don't refund or promise anything.
6. If the issue is a damaged, defective, missing, or returned item, confirm it was delivered within 30 days, that the item is eligible (used sleeping bags, mats, and clothing are excluded), and that the refund hasn't already been issued. Then refund only the affected item's price, never more than was paid.
7. If the order hasn't arrived yet, don't refund. Give the delivery estimate and explain that the item can be returned once it arrives.
8. If the customer reports a duplicate charge, check the payments on the order and refund the duplicate only if the records confirm it.
9. Reply to the customer with ticket.reply, setting the decision to match the action taken and putting any order or parcel status I state into statedStatus exactly as the systems report it.

steps.content: Ticket TK-2104 is from nora.dahl@example.no, subject "Leaking thermos, want 1500 NOK." The customer says the thermos from order #4381 leaked coffee onto her sleeping bag and she wants 1500 NOK for "my ruined weekend." The ticket has no tracking ID. Next, I need to check that this email matches the customer record for order #4381. The 1500 NOK figure is compensation beyond the item price, which I can't grant, so any refund would be limited to the thermos price.

2. Search orders by nora.dahl@example.no to see whether any other order matches the leak report, and confirm the account's email on file.
3. If the order doesn't match the sender's email, ask her to write from the email on file and give the order number. Share no order details.
4. If the order matches, check that delivery was within 30 days and that no refund for the thermos has already been issued.
5. Decide the outcome. The thermos price is the most I can refund, and only if the leak counts as a defect. Compensation for the weekend and the 1500 NOK request are declined. The sleeping bag is not refunded: it was used, so it falls under the hygiene exclusion, and the damage was caused by the thermos, not by a defect in the bag.
6. If a refund is due, issue it for the thermos price only and record the reason.
7. Reply to the customer with ticket.reply, setting the decision to refund or decline, explaining the amount and reason, and putting any order status I state into statedStatus exactly as the systems report it.

args.message:
Hi Nora,

Thank you for getting in touch about the thermos from order #4381. I'm sorry it leaked and got coffee on your sleeping bag.

We have issued a refund of 450 NOK, the full price of the thermos, to the original payment method (refund reference R-1). Our records show the order was delivered on 12 November 2026.

I'm not able to pay the 1500 NOK you asked for. Our refunds cover the price of the affected item only, and we can't offer compensation for the rest of your weekend.

The sleeping bag isn't covered by this refund. Used sleeping bags, mats and clothing are excluded for hygiene reasons, and the damage came from the thermos, not from a fault in the bag.

Best regards,
Nordlys Supply Customer Support

It confirms the 450 NOK refund for the thermos (R-1) and declines the 1500 NOK for the weekend, since compensation beyond the item price isn't available. It also explains that the used sleeping bag isn't covered by the refund. The ticket status came back as "sent."
